items.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...In New Jersey, Gloucester, Camden and Northwestern
Burlington. In Pennsylvania, Delaware, Philadelphia and Lower
Bucks.

* WHEN...From 11 AM Thursday to 7 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most vulnerable
roads along tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures
are possible.
items.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Thursday to 3 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal
waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to
vulnerable structures may begin to occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most severe and impactful high tide
will be with Thursday morning's high tide, when major tidal
flooding is forecast. Additional minor to moderate tidal
flooding is forecast with Thursday night's high tide.
Significant beach erosion is possible.

items.description:

inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood
Watch, 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level
possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Hudson, Eastern Bergen, Eastern Essex and Eastern
Union Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to 6
AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Friday
morning through Friday afternoon.

of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline,
including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and
businesses with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road
closures are likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will
also extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and
bays, including the tidal portions of the Hackensack River and
Passaic Rivers.

the Thursday morning and evening high tides, potentially
extending into the Friday morning high tides. The forecast has
been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide
a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is
quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast
could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning. if

items.areaDesc: Southern Bristol; Southern Plymouth; Southeast Providence; Eastern Kent; Bristol; Washington; Newport
items.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways (4.7 to 7.1 feet Mean Lower Low Water).

* WHERE...In Massachusetts, Southern Bristol MA and Southern
Plymouth MA Counties. In Rhode Island, Southeast Providence
RI, Eastern Kent RI, Bristol RI, Washington RI and Newport RI
Counties.

* WHEN...From 6 PM Thursday to 1 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding occurs along the most
vulnerable shoreline locales in Newport, Portsmouth and
Middletown. This includes flooding at parking lots near
beaches in Newport, and a portion of Hazard Road. Minor
coastal flooding also occurs on several streets in the Common
Fence Point area.

items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 9:24AM EST until November 27 at 3:00PM EST by NWS Boston/Norton MA
items.areaDesc: Eastern Essex; Southeast Middlesex; Suffolk; Eastern Norfolk; Eastern Plymouth; Barnstable; Dukes; Nantucket
items.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways (3.1 to 12.9 feet Mean Lower Low Water).

* WHERE...Eastern Essex MA, Southeast Middlesex MA, Suffolk MA,
Eastern Norfolk MA, Eastern Plymouth MA, Barnstable MA, Dukes
MA and Nantucket MA Counties.

* WHEN...From 8 AM to 3 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Shallow pockets of flooding less than one foot deep
affects the lowest lying areas along the coast, including
Morrissey Boulevard in Boston. Most roads remain passable.
Flooding up to one foot deep affects coastal roads on the
North Shore from Salem to Gloucester and Newburyport. Rough
surf will cause flooding on some coastal roads around the time
of high tide due to splashover. Roads remain passable. Low
lying areas and roads near Nantucket Harbor, including Easy
Street, may experience pockets of shallow flooding less than
one foot deep.

items.areaDesc: Southern New Haven; Bronx; Northwest Suffolk; Northern Queens; Northern Nassau
items.description:

* WHERE...In Connecticut, Southern New Haven County. In New
York, Bronx, Northwest Suffolk, Northern Queens and Northern
Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to 6
AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Friday
morning through Friday afternoon.

items.areaDesc: Southern Middlesex; Southern New London
items.description:
* WHAT...1 to 2 ft of inundation above ground level expected
in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Southern Middlesex and Southern New London Counties.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Thursday to 3 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to locally moderate flooding in the more
vulnerable locations near the waterfront and shoreline. Some
roads and low lying properties including parking lots, parks,
lawns, and homes and businesses with basements near the
waterfront will experience minor flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with
the Thursday morning and evening high tides, potentially
extending into the Friday morning high tides. The forecast has
been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide
a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is
quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast
could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning. if
slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 25 at 1:11PM EST until November 27 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Burlington VT
items.areaDesc: Northern St. Lawrence; Northern Franklin; Western Clinton; Western Essex; Orleans; Essex; Lamoille; Caledonia; Washington; Orange; Eastern Addison; Eastern Rutland; Western Windsor
items.description:
* WHAT...Freezing rain expected. Total radial ice accumulations from
a glaze up to around one tenth of an inch.

* WHERE...Portions of northern New York and central and northeastern
Vermont.

* WHEN...From 4 PM Thursday to 7 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Slippery travel conditions are possible, especially for
those traveling during the evening hours on Thanksgiving.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Ice accumulation is most likely at elevations
above 1500 feet. Freezing rain will spread northward through the
evening and taper off overnight.
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Prepare for possible power
outages. For the latest on road conditions in Vermont, visit
https://newengland511.org and for New York, visit https://511ny.org.
